title: Nurse haunted by six words patient said at 2:30am – right before dying
excerpt: Nurses sometimes see patients in their final moments, which can be very confronting. And one caregiver's experience is so spooky it's keeping people up at night
content:
Nurses sometimes see patients in their final moments, which can be very confronting. And one caregiver's experience is so spooky it's keeping people up at night

08:32, 10 Nov 2026

Nursing is a profession built around helping others and giving back to the community – but it definitely isn’t easy. For many nurses, the job comes with moments they can’t forget, experiences that linger long after a shift ends and, in some cases, haunt them for life. With that in mind, caregivers have come forward to share the incidents from their careers that still give them chills to this day.

‌

‌

The discussion was sparked on TikTok, where a creator called Marisa asked the medical workers for their thoughts. She wrote: “I’m bored. If you’re a nurse, what is the most haunted thing that a patient has ever said to you. I don’t mean ‘somebody is in the room with us’. I mean something that sent chills down your spine.”

‌

The video has since garnered thousands of responses from nurses with strange experiences to share. However, the top comment on the video garnered 387,000 likes and is so creepy that it's been keeping people up at night.

‌

In the viral reply, one nurse said they worked night shifts in a hospital in Louisiana, US, for years – but a single patient has stayed with them ever since.

The commenter explained that the woman – in her late 80s – was “completely alert” and “one of the sweetest patients” they’d ever looked after.

But at around 2.30am, they claimed they found her staring fixedly at an empty chair in the room. When the nurse asked what was wrong, the patient allegedly whispered: “Can you turn it around?”

Asked why, the woman reportedly replied: “The little boy sitting in it keeps smiling at me. I don’t like how many teeth he has.”

‌

The nurse assumed she was hallucinating, turned the chair towards the wall and left the room. However, around 20 minutes later, the patient’s call light went off again – and this time, she was crying.

According to the post, the woman told the nurse: “You shouldn’t have turned his chair around.”

‌

What followed were the scariest six words the hospital worker had apparently heard in her career: When she asked why, the patient said: "Because now he’s standing behind you.”

‌

The commenter said they didn’t turn around – and later, at 3.17am, the patient went into cardiac arrest. They wrote: "We tried everything, but she died. While preparing the room, I noticed the chair was facing the bed again.

‌

"Under her pillow, I found a folded note: 'He’s not a little boy. He just bends down so you can see his face.' Another nurse went pale when I showed her.

To make matters worse, the nurse connected the paranormal experience to another death that occurred "three months earlier".

‌

She recalled: "A seven-year-old girl had died in that same room. Before she passed, she screamed about a man in the corner, someone too tall for the ceiling."

The young girl apparently said the spooky man "wasn't there for her". When asked who he was there for, a colleague whispered "the nurse who always works Thursdays".

‌

Feeling like the spectre must have been talking about her, as she indeed worked Thursdays, the TikTok poster claimed to quit their job.

She added: "On my final shift, the security guard stopped me at the exit. He asked, 'Why does that little boy always follow you down the hallway?' He said he’d been meaning to ask me for months."

‌

Reaction

More than 4,970 people have responded to the story, begging the poster for more details. However, the former nurse claimed they were still trying to come to terms with the spooky occurrence.

They added: "I've tried to find a reasonable explanation for what happened that night... To this day, it's what the security guard said on my last shift that bothers me the most."

‌

It seems the video will now be haunting viewers, too. One said: "I read this at night. On a Thursday. In a hospital where I worked as a nurse... There are stories about child ghosts here (though apparently they just like to pull on people's toes."

Another said: "Nice – now I can't sleep!" And a third joked: "I gotta start thinking of creepy things to say to nurses when I'm old."

Like with any ghost story, you have to choose whether to believe this one or not. If you want to have a peaceful sleep tonight, it may be best to not!
